plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers hang from twining woody vines. They drape pergolas and temple gardens in curtains of violet that can reach over a meter long.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to mid-May in Japan
plants.location: Japan, especially Honshu, in the gardens of Kawachi Fuji and Ashikaga
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise as it climbs. Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise. A single vine can live for more than a century, and the famous Ashikaga Flower Park vine is over 150 years old.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms stand on sturdy stems above bands of fresh green leaves. Fields and borders turn into bright patchworks of color, and the late-season varieties are at their showiest in early May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in the Netherlands
plants.location: The Netherlands, including the bulb fields of Lisse and the Keukenhof gardens
plants.funFact: During the 1630s, tulip bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Dutch 'tulip mania'. It is often called one of the first speculative bubbles in history.

plants.name: Quercus agrifolia
plants.description: Not every bloom is showy. In late spring these evergreen oaks release long, dangling yellow-green catkins that scatter pollen on the wind across hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, roughly March to May, in California
plants.funFact: Oaks are wind-pollinated, so they skip bright petals and nectar. Instead they release huge amounts of light pollen from catkins.
